title: Best Rippling Alternatives for Payroll & HRIS
summary: Compare 8 Rippling alternatives for teams of 20-200 employees, including Warp, Gusto, and Justworks, and how to make the switch.
body_markdown:
**Key takeaways:**


- The best Rippling payroll & HRIS alternatives in 2026 are Warp, Gusto, and Justworks.
- Choose **Warp** if you hire across multiple states and want state tax accounts, filings, and agency notices handled for you.
- Choose **Gusto** for low-cost, single-state payroll. Choose **Justworks** if you want a PEO.


---


Looking for Rippling alternatives? Rippling is a powerful platform, but it was designed as a modular system for companies with dedicated HR and IT teams. If you run a company of 20 to 200 employees, you may be paying for modules you will never turn on, and you still need someone to own compliance.


### **The 8 best Rippling alternatives for small businesses**


#### **1. Warp: best for multi-state compliance automation**


**Best for:** Growing companies hiring across multiple states that want compliance taken off their plate.


Warp is the HRIS & Payroll platform built for ambitious companies who want compliance to run on autopilot. Instead of clicking through clunky dashboards or .gov websites for taxes, Warp's agents open every state tax account, file every payroll form, and resolve every tax notice automatically.


Thousands of fast-growing companies trust Warp to stay compliant while they scale.


**What you get:**


- **Compliance done for you.**[Warp's compliance automation](https://www.warp.co/compliance) covers automated tax filing and state tax registrations on every plan.
- **Benefits brokerage included.** Medical, dental, vision, HSA, FSA and COBRA administration run through Warp's in-house licensed brokerage with no added per-person fee.
- **IT management as an add-on.**[Warp IT](https://www.warp.co/it) bundles Google Workspace provisioning, Okta provisioning and device management, so onboarding and offboarding reach your apps and laptops.
- **Global contractors in 200+ countries** , plus a REST API, CLI and MCP integration included on Starter and Pro.
- **Human support.** Warp reports a 5-minute median response time from a[NYC-based team](https://www.warp.co/support-status) .
- **Migration handled for you.** Warp transfers your data, and offers contract buyouts for teams stuck in a Rippling contract.[See how switching works](https://www.warp.co/switch) .


Sobhan Nejad, COO of Bland AI, says his team switched from Rippling to Warp and found the difference "striking" because Warp kept up with rapid growth without breaking down every week.[Read the Bland story](https://www.warp.co/customers/blandai) .


**Where Warp is not the best fit:** Warp is not the cheapest option on list price. A 10-person team pays more than it would on Gusto. You are paying to stop doing the compliance work yourself, so the math works best when you hire across states or when a missed filing would cost you more than the subscription.


#### **2. Gusto: best for budget-conscious, single-state teams**


**Best for:** teams with straightforward payroll in one or a few states and a tight budget. Per-person pricing stays low at 50 or 100 employees, so check what compliance coverage you get as you add states.


Gusto serves more than 400,000 small businesses and is the default starting point for first-time employers. The interface is clean, the entry price is low, and it connects with most accounting tools.


**What to watch out for:**


- **Multi-state costs more.** Simple is single-state. If you hire in a second state, you move to Plus, and[multi-state hiring brings new registrations and filings](https://www.warp.co/blog/state-nexus-and-payroll-when-hiring-remote-creates-tax-obligations) that you still need to manage.
- **Priority support is an add-on.** Reviewers report that priority phone and chat support on Plus costs another $8 per employee per month.


#### **3. Justworks: best for outsourcing HR through a PEO**


**Best for:** teams that want a professional employer organization (PEO) to handle HR administration, workers' comp, and group benefits.


Justworks is a PEO, making it the closest option on this list for handing HR off to someone else. It also publishes its pricing, which is rare among PEOs. A PEO becomes your co-employer, so the model is different from payroll software, where your company stays the[employer of record](https://www.warp.co/blog/do-startups-really-need-a-peo-or-eor-for-payroll) .


PEO Plus rose from $109 to $124 in June 2026, and the fee excludes health insurance premiums, which are billed separately.


**What Justworks does well:** published pricing, access to large-group benefits for small teams, and phone support that reviewers rate highly.


**What to consider:**


- **Pricing moves.** Both PEO tiers took double-digit list increases between mid-2025 and mid-2026, and benefits costs can change at renewal. Understanding[how health plan funding models work](https://www.warp.co/blog/level-funded-vs-fully-insured-vs-self-insured-health-plans) helps you anticipate that.
- **Co-employment.** Your employees are technically employed by Justworks.
- **The jump from Payroll to PEO is large.** A 10-person team pays $130 a month on Payroll and $790 on PEO Basic, so decide whether you actually need the PEO before comparing.


#### **4. Deel: best for global hiring**


**Best for:** companies hiring full-time employees in other countries.


Deel started in contractor payments and expanded into employer of record (EOR), global payroll and US payroll. If your next ten hires are abroad, it is built for that.


**What to consider:** EOR fees are platform charges only, before salary, taxes and benefits. If your hires are mostly in the US, a US-focused platform is usually simpler.


#### **5. ADP RUN: best for an established provider with a quote-based model**


**Best for:** small businesses with 1 to 49 employees that want a large, long-standing payroll provider and are comfortable getting a quote.


ADP RUN is ADP's small-business payroll and HR product. ADP does not publish RUN pricing. Third-party reports put entry pricing near $79 per month plus $4 per employee for RUN Essential, and estimate a 10-person business at $150 to $250 a month once add-ons are included. One third-party guide also reports a $12 per state per month surcharge for multi-state payroll, so confirm that in your quote.


**What to consider:** ADP brings scale, tax filing support and HR add-ons. The tradeoff is pricing opacity and a quote process, which is the same friction that sends many teams away from Rippling. Ask for an itemized quote that lists base fees, per-employee fees, state fees and add-ons.


#### **6. BambooHR: best for HR-led teams that want a simple HRIS**


**Best for:** teams that want a people-ops system of record first and payroll second.


BambooHR is an HR information system (HRIS) with a reputation for being easy to use. Payroll is not part of the base product. It is a separate add-on that works for US employees only, and BambooHR does not publish its price.


**What to consider:**


- **A small-team floor.** At the $250 minimum, a five-person company pays at least $50 per employee per month before adding payroll.
- **Payroll is separate.** Payroll and benefits administration are add-ons with unpublished pricing, so request a bundled quote.
- **Compliance is not the focus.** Ask who handles state registrations and agency notices before you rely on the payroll add-on for multi-state hiring.


#### **7. Paylocity: best for mid-market teams that want a quote-based HCM suite**


**Best for:** companies heading toward 50 or more employees that want payroll, HR and talent tools from one vendor.


**What to consider:**


- **Mid-market focus.** Paylocity is built for companies of roughly 50 to 5,000 employees, so a 15-person startup is usually below its sweet spot.
- **Quote-only pricing.** Ask for an itemized quote that covers implementation, integrations, data migration and any transaction fees


#### **8. Insperity: best for a premium full-service PEO**


**Best for:** companies with at least five employees that want a PEO to run HR, payroll and benefits.


**What to consider:**


- **Co-employment.** As with any PEO, Insperity becomes your co-employer, so you give up some control over benefits and policies.
- **Cost.** Ten employees at the reported range is about $1,500 to $2,100 a month, versus $790 for Justworks PEO Basic.


### **How to choose the right Rippling alternative**


**Choose Warp if:**


- You hire across multiple states, or plan to in the next year.
- You want state tax accounts, filings and notices handled for you.
- You want to be your own Employer of Record, under your own EIN.
- You want transparent pricing and a migration handled by the vendor.


**Choose Gusto if:**


- You have 10 to 50 employees, mostly in one or a few states.
- Budget is your primary concern and your payroll is straightforward.


**Choose Justworks if:**


- You want to outsource HR administration and accept co-employment.
- Large-group benefits matter for recruiting and you have no HR hire.


**Five questions to ask any vendor before you sign**


1. Who opens our state tax accounts when we hire in a new state?
2. Who responds when a state agency sends a notice, and how fast?
3. What does the contract say if we miss a filing and get penalized?
4. What will our bill be at 25, 50 and 100 employees after add-ons?
5. What is the contract term, and what does it cost to leave?


The answers to the first three usually separate platforms that give you tools from platforms that do the work. Before you commit, read about[common payroll mistakes](https://www.warp.co/blog/common-payroll-mistakes) that turn into penalties.


### **How to switch from Rippling: a checklist for teams of 20 to 200 employees**


You can switch payroll providers at any time, including mid-year. The old rule of thumb is to move on January 1, but a mid-year switch is also possible.


1. **Read your Rippling agreement.** Note the term, renewal date, and notice period. Some providers, including Warp, offer a contract buyout for teams stuck in a Rippling contract.
2. **Choose a cutover date.** Start the new provider at the beginning of a pay period. Many teams prefer the start of a quarter because it keeps quarterly tax filings clean.
3. **Export your data.** Gather employee records, year-to-date payroll, pay history, state tax account numbers, PTO balances and benefits enrollments.
4. **Ask how tax accounts transfer.** Confirm who handles state account access and agency notices during the overlap.
5. **Plan the benefits handoff.** If you are keeping the same health insurance or 401(k), someone has to coordinate the change in payroll deductions.
6. **Verify before go-live.** Compare the new provider's test payroll against your last Rippling run and resolve any differences before the first live payroll.
7. **Tell your team, then close the old account.** Let employees know what changes, and cancel Rippling only after the first payroll and the next tax filing reconcile.


**What switching looks like with Warp.** Most companies finish the move in 1 to 2 weeks, with free, white-glove migration support. Warp imports year-to-date payroll, employee records, tax filings, pay history and benefits enrollment, and has migrated thousands of companies from providers including ADP, Gusto, Rippling and Paylocity. See[how switching works](https://www.warp.co/switch) or read the[full step-by-step guide to switching payroll providers](https://www.warp.co/blog/how-to-switch-payroll-providers-in-2026-a-step-by-step-guide-for-startups) .


### **Bottom line**


If you are comparing Rippling alternatives, start with the question that matters most: who does the compliance work when you hire in a new state? For multi-state startups that want it handled automatically, Warp is built for exactly that. Gusto works for budget-conscious single-state teams, Justworks for teams that want a PEO, Deel for global hiring, and ADP RUN for teams that want an established name.
